correctness.rationale: For every m>=4 and s>=m-1, full-rank CountSketch maps require at least m-1 occupied active buckets. Zero collisions give identity Gram; one equal-sign collision kills a zero-sum difference; one opposite-sign collision gives an explicit orthogonal eigen-decomposition with eigenvalues 2,1 (m-3 copies),2/m. QR preserves the nonzero sketch condition number on isometric A. Independent occupancy/sign counting yields exact probabilities and the ratio of falling factorials establishes the Poisson birthday window. The included executable exhaustively checked 48,160 signs-and-hashes configurations (four cases), their eigenvalues, and a separate suite of QR-preconditioner instances; numeric checks are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-dimensional distribution of QR conditioning, especially the rank-preserving opposite-sign collision with exact sqrt(m) conditioning and its explicit critical-window mass, is not stated or implied by the examined sources. The generic quadratic lower bound, the preconditioner algorithm, and the three-row rank-loss special case are acknowledged as older work. Comparisons are statement-level rather than title-level; residual bibliographic risk remains.
residual_risks: The complete text of arXiv:2112.10987 was not inspected; specialized spectral statements could be present.
Very similar conditional spectra may appear in unindexed randomized numerical linear-algebra papers, even if no record matches the chosen terminology.
The event probabilities follow classical birthday occupancy combinatorics; only their rigorous spectral-conditioned interpretation is asserted as a distinct mathematical claim.
The three-row special case of rank-loss had already been considered elsewhere and is excluded from the new quantified domain.

value.rationale: The mean-zero hyperplane is canonically the range of a connected tree incidence matrix, a natural linear constraint. This all-dimensional calculation measures a concrete and practically interpretable loss of preconditioning reliability on an exactly isometric system. The distinction between a nonsingular but sqrt(m)-ill-conditioned one-collision branch and catastrophic rank loss, with exact finite probabilities and sharp nondegenerate Poisson-window masses, provides a motivated spectral benchmark not supplied by a generic birthday count or OSE row-order lower bound. It does not claim improved algorithms or generic conditioning bounds.
